scenes.narration: RMiT says the bank remains accountable for all risks from third-party service providers. The board and senior management must oversee providers of critical technology.

scenes.heading: Due diligence, before and during
scenes.narration: Banks check a provider before onboarding and throughout the relationship, and work towards continuous monitoring of the provider's cyber posture.

scenes.heading: Approval for material outsourcing
scenes.narration: Under BNM's outsourcing policy document, a bank needs BNM's written approval before entering a new material outsourcing arrangement or significantly changing an existing one.

scenes.heading: Cloud with care
scenes.narration: Before adopting cloud, banks assess risks such as location, multi-tenancy, lock-in and exit. They must keep ownership and control of customer data and the encryption keys.

scenes.heading: Train the provider too
scenes.narration: Service agreements should require providers to join the bank's security awareness programme where appropriate, and outsourced providers must train their staff on customer information.

cards.title: First critical system on public cloud
cards.caption: Based on RMiT paragraphs 10.50, 10.52, 17.1 and 17.5.

items.label: Risk assessment
items.detail: Cover deployment model, migration, location, multi-tenancy, lock-in, configuration, cyber exposure, exit and responsibilities.

items.label: Readiness confirmation
items.detail: Signed by the CISO, a senior management officer or the board or committee chair, in BNM's format.

items.label: Independent review
items.detail: Third-party pre-implementation review, deeper where customer data or cross-border transfers are involved.

items.label: Consult BNM
items.detail: Before first-time adoption; proceed only once risks are addressed to BNM's satisfaction.

items.label: Keep control
items.detail: Retain ownership and control of customer data and cryptographic keys; include the roadmap in the outsourcing plan.

cards.question: Bukit Kenanga plans to host its first critical system on a public cloud. What does RMiT require before adoption?
options: Consult BNM, after a risk assessment, a readiness confirmation and a third-party pre-implementation review
Notify BNM within 30 days after the system goes live
Obtain approval from the PDP Commissioner
Nothing, if the cloud provider holds an international security certification
cards.explanation: Paragraph 17.1 requires consultation with BNM before the first-time adoption of public cloud for critical systems, supported by the risk assessment, readiness confirmation and independent review. Later adoptions may move to notification under 17.2 if conditions are met.

cards.title: What a service agreement must cover
cards.body:
RMiT paragraph 10.48 sets the minimum for a service level agreement with a technology provider. Among others:

- **Access rights for BNM** and parties the bank appoints to examine records and data.
- **Prior notice** of substantial **sub-contracting**.
- A written undertaking on **secrecy**, binding even after the contract ends.
- **Disaster recovery, backup**, uptime objectives and **exit** arrangements so data can be recovered in time.
- **Prompt notice** to the bank of service disruptions or cyber incidents affecting it or its customer data, including at sub-contractors.
- Key provider staff kept **certified**, and provider participation in the bank's **security awareness programme** where appropriate.

MCIPD adds for providers handling customer information: vetting of personnel, **regular training**, breach reporting within an agreed time, return or destruction of data at the end, audit rights, a **non-disclosure undertaking**, and a bank review **at least once every two years**.

cards.title: The amended PDPA in six terms
cards.prompt: Match each PDPA term to its meaning, as the Act now stands.

pairs.right: The person who processes personal data or controls or authorises its processing, such as the bank
Processes data only on the controller's behalf; must now comply with the Security Principle
Appointed by controllers and processors, accountable for compliance; the Commissioner is notified
Practical steps to protect data, including reliability, integrity and competence of staff with access
Includes health data, religious or political beliefs, alleged offences and biometric data
Allowed to places with substantially similar law or adequate protection, or under listed exceptions

cards.title: How hard to watch each provider
cards.caption: A practical way to set oversight intensity. RMiT asks for continuous monitoring of critical providers' cyber posture.

items.label: Critical, little data
items.detail: Network or data centre provider: resilience tests, uptime SLAs, incident alerts.

items.label: Critical, much data
items.detail: Core or cloud provider: deepest due diligence, continuous monitoring, BNM approval or consultation.

items.label: Low, little data
items.detail: Office supplies: standard contract and periodic review.

items.label: Low, much data
items.detail: Printing or archiving vendor: vetting, training, secrecy undertaking, two-yearly review.

lines.text: BNM won't ask whether we have policies. They'll ask for evidence that they work.
I have the MCIPD independent review from last year, the breach register and the annual awareness survey on customer information.
Cyber drill report to the board, red team results, phishing simulation trends, and proof that CERT can be reached at 3 am.
Training records for every agent, plus our scam call scripts. And our outsourced overflow team finished the awareness module this year.
And the board? We need proof that directors took part in cyber training too.

cards.title: The provider that will not share
cards.situation: Bukit Kenanga's managed SOC provider is renewing its contract. It refuses to tell the bank about cyber incidents in its own environment unless they are 'confirmed material', and says its analysts are too busy to join the bank's awareness programme. Procurement wants to sign because the price is low.

choices.text: Insist on prompt notice of disruptions and cyber incidents affecting the bank or its data, BNM access rights and awareness participation; escalate if the provider refuses
choices.outcome: Right. RMiT paragraph 10.48 makes these service agreement terms, and the bank needs prompt provider alerts to meet its own two-hour BNM clock.

choices.text: Sign, but ask for a quarterly summary of incidents instead
choices.outcome: A quarterly summary cannot support a two-hour notification to BNM or a fast response. It falls short of RMiT's prompt-notice requirement.

choices.text: Sign as proposed; the provider is responsible for its own security
choices.outcome: RMiT is explicit that the bank remains accountable for risks from its providers. Accepting blind spots breaks that duty.

cards.title: Cycles BNM will check
cards.caption: From RMiT, the NCII code (Appendix 12) and MCIPD. NCII items apply only to designated banks.

items.label: Awareness for all staff
items.detail: RMiT 15.1; NCII banks also review the awareness programme at least annually.

items.label: Cyber drill
items.detail: Tests the incident plan and out-of-band channel; results go to the board.

items.label: MCIPD independent review
items.detail: Of customer information controls, ordered by senior management.

items.label: Outsourced provider review
items.detail: Confirms the provider protects customer information as contracted.

items.label: Red team exercise
items.detail: Realistic attack simulation on the bank's infrastructure.

items.label: Breach report retention
items.detail: Investigation reports kept from the date tabled to the board.

cards.question: Since the 2024 PDPA amendments took effect, which statement about data protection officers is correct?
options: Both data controllers and data processors must appoint one or more DPOs and notify the Commissioner of the controller's appointment
Only banks with more than 1,000 customers must appoint a DPO
Appointing a DPO transfers the bank's PDPA duties to that officer personally
DPOs are appointed by BNM for each licensed bank
cards.explanation: Section 12A requires controllers and processors to appoint DPOs accountable to them, and the controller to notify the Commissioner. The appointment does not discharge the controller or processor from their duties under the Act.

cards.title: Real case: the data centre move that needed approval
cards.body:
On **22 July 2024** BNM imposed an administrative monetary penalty of **RM88,000** on **Bank of China (Malaysia) Berhad**, published on 23 August 2024.

The bank had **moved two core banking systems to new data centres** in December 2022 and February 2023 **without BNM's prior approval**. BNM treated the relocation as a **significant modification** of an approved **material outsourcing arrangement**, because it could materially change the level or type of risk. The Outsourcing policy document requires written approval before such a change.

BNM traced the breach to **gaps in oversight of outsourcing** and in internal policies. The bank responded with periodic reviews of its outsourcing arrangements and better coordination with group functions.

**Your lesson**: technology changes made by a provider or group function can trigger BNM approval or consultation duties. Ask early.

cards.front: Who must get annual cyber awareness?
cards.back: All staff, under RMiT 15.1, plus third-party providers where appropriate; effectiveness must be measured.
Must complete cyber awareness training before getting access to the NCII entity's assets.
Within 2 hours of confirmation, by the central email with the cyber incident scoring form.
More than 1,000 affected customers; notify BNM immediately.

cards.front: PDPA penalty for breaking the principles
cards.back: A fine up to RM1 million, prison up to 3 years, or both (section 5(2)).
Join cybersecurity awareness and training (8.4(c)) and get regular training on technology developments (15.3).

cards.title: Stage five take-aways
items: The bank stays accountable for risks from third-party providers; due diligence runs before and during the engagement.
Service agreements must give BNM access, require prompt incident notice and secrecy, and bring providers into awareness training where appropriate.
BNM's written approval is needed before new material outsourcing or a significant change; first-time public cloud for critical systems needs prior consultation.
The amended PDPA binds processors to the Security Principle, requires DPOs, and allows transfers abroad only on its listed grounds.
Readiness means evidence: training records and effectiveness results, drills, red team results, reviews, registers and board reports.

cards.prompt: Which outside companies handle data or systems for your team? Do you know who manages each relationship, and how they would tell your bank about an incident?

quiz.question: Under RMiT paragraph 10.46, who remains accountable for risks arising from a bank's third-party technology providers?
options: The provider, once the contract and service level agreement have been signed by both parties
BNM, as the approving authority
The provider's own regulator in its home country
The bank itself, overseen by its board and senior management
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 10.46 states that the financial institution remains accountable for all risks arising from engaging third-party providers, with the board and senior management exercising oversight.

quiz.question: Which term must a bank's service agreement with a technology provider contain under RMiT paragraph 10.48?
options: The provider must store all data only on the bank's premises and never use sub-contractors
Prompt notice to the bank of disruptions or cyber incidents affecting it
The provider must be a Malaysian-owned company
The provider must report its incidents directly to BNM instead
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 10.48(g) requires prompt disclosure and notification to the bank of service disruptions or cyber incidents, including in sub-contractors' environments, so the bank can update BNM.

quiz.question: Under BNM's Outsourcing policy document, when does a bank need BNM's written approval?
options: Only after a material arrangement has run for one year and passed its first annual review
Before a new material arrangement or a significant change to one
For every outsourcing arrangement, however small
Only when the provider is located outside Malaysia
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 12.1 requires BNM's written approval before a new material outsourcing arrangement or a significant modification to an existing one, as the Bank of China (Malaysia) case showed.

quiz.question: Which risk must a bank's assessment before cloud adoption specifically address under RMiT paragraph 10.50?
options: Multi-tenancy or data co-mingling
The provider's marketing budget
The bank's dividend policy
The number of branches the bank operates
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 10.50 lists risks including the deployment model, migration, location, multi-tenancy, vendor lock-in, security configuration, cyber exposure, termination, demarcation of responsibilities and ongoing regulatory compliance.

quiz.question: When using cloud services, what must a bank retain under RMiT paragraph 10.52?
options: Physical possession of the cloud provider's servers in a data centre located in Malaysia
Ownership and control of customer data and the encryption keys
A copy of the provider's source code
The right to appoint the provider's directors
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 10.52 requires safeguards against unauthorised access, including keeping ownership, control and management of customer and proprietary data and the related cryptographic keys.

quiz.question: Under the amended PDPA, which Personal Data Protection Principle must a data processor comply with when processing on a controller's behalf?
options: The Security Principle
The Notice and Choice Principle
The Access Principle
The Retention Principle
quiz.explanation: Section 5(1a), added by the amendment, requires a data processor to comply with the Security Principle in section 9. The other principles remain duties of the data controller.

quiz.question: What does the PDPA's Security Principle expressly ask data controllers to consider about staff?
options: Measures for the reliability, integrity and competence of staff with access
The salary bands and seniority of every member of staff who has access to personal data
The nationality of staff with access to personal data
Whether staff have personal social media accounts
quiz.explanation: Section 9(1)(d) lists measures for the reliability, integrity and competence of personnel who access personal data, which is one reason banks train staff on data protection.

quiz.question: Under MCIPD, how often must a bank review an outsourced service provider that handles customer information?
options: At least once every five years
Only when the contract is renewed
Only after a breach at the provider
At least once every two years
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 12.9 requires a review at least once every two years to confirm the provider meets its contractual obligations to safeguard customer information.

quiz.question: Under RMiT Appendix 12, when must new employees of an NCII-designated bank complete cyber security awareness training?
options: Before being granted access to the NCII entity's assets
Within their first year of employment
Only if they work in the IT department
After their probation period ends
quiz.explanation: Appendix 12 paragraph 6.3.3 requires all new employees to complete cyber awareness training before getting access to the NCII entity's assets.

quiz.question: What is the maximum penalty under section 5(2) of the PDPA for a data controller that breaches the Personal Data Protection Principles?
options: A fine up to RM1 million, imprisonment up to three years, or both
A fine up to RM250,000, imprisonment up to two years, or both
A fine up to RM100,000 only
A fine up to RM5 million, imprisonment up to ten years, or both
quiz.explanation: Section 5(2) sets a fine not exceeding one million ringgit, imprisonment up to three years, or both. RM250,000 and two years is the penalty for failing to notify the Commissioner under section 12B(1).

bank.question: Bukit Kenanga's board approves a technology risk appetite. Which further step does RMiT paragraph 8.1 require as part of that approval?
options: Approve each new IT system purchase above RM100,000 before the contract is signed
Approve risk tolerances, risk owners and key risk indicators
Delegate the risk appetite entirely to the CISO
Submit the risk appetite to BNM for approval
bank.explanation: Paragraph 8.1 asks the board to approve tolerances, identify risk owners and criteria for accepting residual risk, ensure key risk indicators and adequate resources, and review the appetite regularly. BNM approval is not required.

bank.question: What period must the IT and cybersecurity strategic plans approved by the board cover under RMiT?
options: No less than three years
Exactly one financial year
No less than ten years
The remaining term of the current CEO
bank.explanation: Paragraph 8.2(a) requires the board to approve and review IT and cybersecurity strategic plans covering a period of no less than three years.

bank.question: Unless RMiT states otherwise, how often must IT-related frameworks, policies and guidelines be reviewed?
options: Every month by the cross-functional committee
At least once every three years, with depth matched to complexity and risk changes
Only when BNM issues a new policy document
Every five years at the strategic plan refresh
bank.explanation: Paragraph 8.2(d) requires reviews at least once every three years unless otherwise stated, with depth commensurate with complexity and changes in the risk environment.

bank.question: A director says: 'Board members do not need cyber training; we have a technology expert on the committee.' Which RMiT provisions show this is wrong?
options: Paragraph 10.32 on downtime and paragraph 12.5 on SMS links
Paragraph 11.6 on red teaming and paragraph 17.1 on cloud
Paragraph 14.1 on data centre resilience assessments
Paragraphs 8.4(c) and 15.3
bank.explanation: RMiT requires the board itself to take part in cybersecurity awareness and training (8.4(c)) and to receive regular training on technology developments (15.3). Having one expert member is a separate requirement for the committee.

bank.question: Which body must ensure the internal technology audit function is effective, including the competence of audit staff, under RMiT?
options: The cross-functional technology committee
The security operations centre
The board audit committee
The bank's external cloud provider
bank.explanation: Paragraph 8.5 makes the board audit committee responsible for an effective internal technology audit function, including audit staff competence, scope, frequency and prompt closure of gaps.

bank.question: RMiT section 15.1 allows banks to include third-party service providers in training 'where appropriate'. Which other RMiT paragraph supports this through contracts?
options: Paragraph 10.48(i), on providers joining the awareness programme
Paragraph 11.6, requiring a realistic red team exercise at least once every three years
Paragraph 10.32, on maximum downtime for critical systems
Paragraph 8.3, on the board technology committee
bank.explanation: Paragraph 15.1 refers to paragraph 10.48(i), which makes participation in the bank's awareness and education programme a service agreement requirement where appropriate.

bank.question: Senior management at Bukit Kenanga wants to show BNM the annual awareness programme meets RMiT. Which evidence best fits paragraph 15.1?
options: Current content, completion records for all staff and evidence of behaviour change
A certificate from the vendor that sold the e-learning platform confirming it meets international standards
A list of staff who attended induction three years ago
Minutes showing the board approved the training budget
bank.explanation: Paragraph 15.1 asks for adequate, regular, at least annual education reflecting evolving threats, with effectiveness measured. Vendor certificates, old induction lists and budget approvals do not show that.

bank.question: A bank's CISO also leads several group functions abroad. Under RMiT, when is this acceptable?
options: Never; the CISO must hold no other role anywhere in the group, in Malaysia or abroad, at any time
Only if BNM appoints the CISO directly
Only if the CISO reports to the head of IT operations
When independence and competence are not impaired and the CISO stays accountable
bank.explanation: RMiT's footnote to paragraph 9.4 allows a CISO to draw on group expertise and hold other roles if independence and competence are not impaired, while remaining the accountable contact with BNM.

bank.question: Bukit Kenanga's SOC currently monitors only internet-facing systems. Which RMiT requirement does this fall short of?
options: The SOC must be located outside Malaysia
The scope of monitoring must cover all critical systems, including supporting infrastructure
The SOC must be outsourced to a BNM-approved provider
The SOC must report every alert directly to BNM
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.9(b) requires monitoring to cover all critical systems and their supporting infrastructure, supported by a competent SOC with the right tools.

bank.question: Which security approach does RMiT describe as requiring every user, inside or outside the network, to be authenticated, authorised and validated before access?
options: Perimeter trust
Zero trust
Single sign-on
Air-gapping
bank.explanation: RMiT's footnote to paragraph 11.3(d) describes zero-trust principles as requiring all users, inside or outside the network, to be authenticated, authorised and validated before access.

bank.question: A contractor's access to production servers is set to expire automatically at the end of the agreed maintenance window. Which RMiT access principle is this?
options: Dual authorisation
Time-bound access
Deny all by default
Data loss prevention
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.54(c) requires time-bound access that restricts access to a specific period based on the nature of the work.

bank.question: Which statement about online credentials matches RMiT paragraph 10.54(f)?
options: A team may share one credential if the team leader approves
Credentials may be shared during system outages
Each online credential must be uniquely linked to a single user for clear accountability
Shared credentials are acceptable for read-only access
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.54(f)(iii) requires each online credential to be uniquely linked to one user so that access to confidential IT assets is accountable.

bank.question: An internal audit finds that Bukit Kenanga cannot tell which staff viewed a celebrity customer's account last month. Which MCIPD requirement is most clearly at risk?
options: The requirement to publish a privacy notice on the website and in every branch of the bank
Prompt detection of unauthorised access and unusual frequent viewing
The requirement to keep complaint records for seven years
The requirement to consult BNM before using public cloud
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.23 requires prompt detection of unauthorised access and unusual frequent viewing; without usable audit trails the bank cannot meet it. MCIPD's guidance mentions audit trail reviews and random checks.

bank.question: What does MCIPD require banks to do about the access rights of staff who change roles or leave?
options: Regularly review access rights and revoke them immediately when no longer needed
Keep access active for 90 days in case the staff member returns
Transfer the access rights to the staff member's replacement
Review access rights only during the annual audit
bank.explanation: MCIPD requires regular reviews of staff access rights and immediate revocation where access is no longer required, consistent with RMiT's least privilege and periodic access matrix reviews.

bank.question: In the 2026 Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Berhad case, what did BNM say the RMiT breaches were attributed to?
options: Inadequate cybersecurity controls and incident response
Late submission of cash threshold reports
Failure to publish product disclosure sheets
Breaching the single counterparty exposure limit
bank.explanation: BNM's release said the RMiT and MCIPD breaches, found after an external threat actor gained unauthorised access, were attributed to inadequate cybersecurity controls and incident response.

bank.question: Under the NCII code in RMiT Appendix 12, what must an IT acceptable use policy cover?
options: Only the list of approved software vendors and the prices the bank has negotiated with each of them
Acceptable, prohibited and personal use, privacy, violations, remote work and BYOD
Only rules for the use of company cars and phones
Only the bank's social media marketing guidelines
bank.explanation: Appendix 12 paragraph 7.1.1 lists acceptable, prohibited and personal use, privacy expectations, reporting violations, remote work and a BYOD policy, and staff must be trained on it.

bank.question: What did the September 2026 reissue of RMiT add for banks designated under the Cyber Security Act 2024?
options: A new licensing regime for cloud providers
A ban on all use of public cloud for critical systems
Appendix 12, a code of practice for NCII entities designated by BNM in the banking and finance sector
A requirement for every bank to appoint a NACSA officer to its board
bank.explanation: The reissued RMiT added Appendix 12, which together with the relevant RMiT requirements forms the code of practice for NCII entities designated by BNM under the Cyber Security Act 2024.

bank.question: Bukit Kenanga still uses unencrypted SMS one-time passwords for high-value transfers. Which RMiT requirement is it most likely failing?
options: Removing hyperlinks from customer SMS messages
Deploying MFA technology and channels more secure than unencrypted SMS for financial transactions
Running the annual cyber drill with the board
Consulting BNM before using public cloud
bank.explanation: Appendix 3 requires MFA for financial transactions to resist phishing and use technology and channels more secure than unencrypted SMS. The SMS link rule is a different control.

bank.question: Where a bank uses OTPs, which feature does RMiT Appendix 3 require?
options: It is generated on the customer's device and bound to the payee and amount
It is sent by email as well as SMS, so that the customer has a backup if one channel fails
It stays valid for 24 hours so customers are not rushed
It is generated on the bank's server and shown on the website
bank.explanation: Appendix 3 requires dynamic, time-bound OTPs bound to transaction details and generated on the customer's device, not the bank's server, to reduce manipulation risk.

bank.question: A customer wants to add a new 'favourite' payee in the app. What does RMiT Appendix 3 require?
options: MFA only for the first transfer to the new payee
MFA when registering the favourite payee and for all later transfers to that payee
No authentication, because favourites are trusted
Approval from a branch manager before the payee is saved
bank.explanation: Appendix 3 requires MFA for financial and high-risk non-financial transactions, including registering a favourite beneficiary and all subsequent transfers to that beneficiary.

bank.question: A new digital banking customer asks why her daily transfer limit is low. What does RMiT Appendix 3 say about default limits for new customers?
options: Default limits must be fixed at RM50,000 for all customers, whatever their profile or how long they have banked with us
Limits are set by BNM for each customer
They should be conservatively low, for example RM1,000 a day, and changeable securely
New customers cannot transfer money for six months
bank.explanation: Appendix 3 sets a conservatively low default limit for new customers, giving RM1,000 per day as an example, with the option to change it through secure channels such as MFA online or at branches.

bank.question: Which signals does RMiT Appendix 11 require fraud analytics to consider when the customer has just registered MFA on a new device and then makes many transfers to new payees?
options: Only transactions above RM100,000, because smaller transfers are below the fraud threshold BNM sets
Only transfers to overseas accounts
Risky account changes followed by many debits to new payees soon after
Only transactions made outside office hours
bank.explanation: Appendix 11 lists elevated-risk activities such as MFA registration on a new device, followed by patterns such as high-volume debits to new beneficiaries within a day or the next few days.

bank.question: What must a bank do when a customer's online banking access is restricted because of suspected fraud, under RMiT Appendix 11?
options: Keep the account locked until the customer visits BNM
Close the account and open a new one automatically
Promptly notify the customer with guidance to restore access after robust verification
Inform the customer only if the customer complains
bank.explanation: Appendix 11 paragraph 4 requires prompt notification with guidance so the customer can restore access subject to robust verification; consent is needed before device profiling.

bank.question: RMiT paragraph 12.5(c) addresses a common scam. What must banks provide?
options: Practical ways for customers to check that a call from the bank is genuine
A list of all staff phone numbers on the website so that customers can call anyone back directly
Recordings of every call sent to customers by email
A promise that the bank will never call customers
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12.5(c) requires practical ways for customers to verify the authenticity of calls made by the bank or its appointed outsourced service providers.

bank.question: Bukit Kenanga's contact centre has long queues on Friday nights, the peak time for scam reports. Which RMiT requirement is most directly engaged?
options: Running a red team exercise every three years
Keeping critical system logs for three years
Retaining breach investigation reports for seven years
Keeping the contact centre adequately resourced and effective to help customers in distress
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12.8(b) requires an adequately resourced, effective contact centre for customers in distress, alongside a self-service kill switch and timely restoration of access.

bank.question: Under BNM's policy document on victims of unauthorised e-banking transactions, what must banks regularly remind customers to do?
options: Change their account number every year and register a new mobile number with the bank each time
Visit a branch every six months to confirm their identity
Share their passwords only with bank staff who call them
Check alerts promptly, verify bank messages and read the security tips
bank.explanation: Paragraph 8.1 requires current safety tips and regular reminders to check alerts and statements, verify bank messages and read security warnings before sharing confidential information.

bank.question: A bank's email system is compromised during a ransomware attack. Which RMiT requirement helps the CERT keep coordinating?
options: Default transfer limits for new customers
An annual outsourcing plan submitted to BNM
A conservative technology risk appetite
A secure, reliable out-of-band communication infrastructure, tested regularly in cyber drills
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.15 requires out-of-band communication for internal and external stakeholders if primary channels fail, and paragraph 11.16 requires it to be tested in drills.

bank.question: Under the BCM policy document, what must a bank do after its initial cyber incident notification to BNM as more facts come to light?
options: Wait for BNM to request an update
Send nothing further until the investigation closes
Inform only the PDP Commissioner of new facts
Progressively update BNM with the latest information
bank.explanation: The BCM document requires the bank to progressively update BNM as information on the disruption changes, so that BNM can respond or intervene where needed.

bank.question: In the BCM policy document, when does the two-hour cyber incident clock start?
options: When the first customer complaint is received
When the board is informed
When the forensic investigation is complete
On confirmation, after a preliminary investigation shows the incident is cyber-related
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.5 runs the two hours from confirmation; its footnote describes confirmation as following a preliminary investigation into whether the incident is cyber-centric, such as ransomware, DDoS or a data leak.

bank.question: An NCII-designated bank must nominate people responsible for notifying cyber security incidents to NACSA. How many does RMiT Appendix 12 require?
options: One authorised person
Five authorised persons
No specific number
Three authorised persons
bank.explanation: Appendix 12 paragraph 18.1.4(c) requires the NCII entity to nominate three authorised persons for cyber security incident notification under the Cyber Security Act 2024.

bank.question: A customer information breach is caused by a staff member deliberately selling data, affecting 40 customers. Which MCIPD duty applies even though fewer than 1,000 customers are affected?
options: No duty beyond internal handling, because the breach is below the significant scale threshold of 1,000 customers
Only an entry in the breach register
Sending the investigation report to BNM within one working day of tabling
Only a notice on the bank's website
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.20 requires the report to be submitted where the breach causes or may cause significant harm, exceeds 1,000 customers, or involves a deliberate attempt at unauthorised disclosure. Deliberate selling meets the third limb.

bank.question: Who must confirm a bank's assessment that a customer information breach causes or is likely to cause significant harm, under MCIPD?
options: The designated officer of sufficient senior ranking named under MCIPD paragraph 9.2
The branch manager where the breach happened
The external auditor
The affected customer
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.13 requires the significant harm assessment to be confirmed by the designated senior officer under paragraph 9.2, who also signs off the investigation report.

bank.question: Under MCIPD, who must carry out and oversee the root-cause investigation of a customer information breach?
options: The staff member who caused the breach
The business unit where it occurred, without independent oversight
A competent party, overseen by a party independent of the business unit where the breach occurred
BNM's Consumer and Market Conduct Department
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.18 requires a competent party to investigate, overseen by a party independent of the relevant business unit, and to determine remedial actions.

bank.question: A breach involves customer information Bukit Kenanga received from another bank through a permitted disclosure. What must Bukit Kenanga do?
options: Leave all notifications and the investigation to the other bank, since the data originally belonged to it
Delete the data and take no further action
Promptly notify the other bank, and investigate and report itself
Notify only the customers, not the other bank
bank.explanation: Paragraphs 11.6 and 11.22 require the institution where the breach occurred to notify the affected provider promptly and to carry out the investigation and reporting duties.

bank.question: Under the amended PDPA, what is the consequence for a data controller that fails to notify the Commissioner of a personal data breach as section 12B(1) requires?
options: It commits an offence punishable by a fine up to RM250,000, imprisonment up to two years, or both
It receives an automatic warning letter with no further penalty
It loses its banking licence
It must pay compensation of RM1,000 to each data subject
bank.explanation: Section 12B(3) makes failure to notify under 12B(1) an offence with a fine not exceeding RM250,000, imprisonment up to two years, or both.

bank.question: After customer credentials are exposed in an incident, which additional measures does RMiT paragraph 12.9 require?
options: Closing all affected accounts permanently and asking the customers to open new accounts at a branch
Charging affected customers for replacement cards
Waiting for customers to report fraud before acting
Closer monitoring, customer notices and reissued credentials or cards
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12.9 requires closer monitoring of affected accounts, notifying affected customers with information to protect themselves, and revoking and reissuing compromised credentials or payment instruments where needed.

bank.question: Bukit Kenanga has already consulted BNM on its first critical system on public cloud with no concerns raised. What usually applies when it moves a second critical system to public cloud?
options: No contact with BNM at all
A fresh consultation, every time, without exception
Approval from the PDP Commissioner instead of BNM
Notification to BNM with updated information, if the RMiT conditions for subsequent adoption are met
bank.explanation: Paragraph 17.2 allows notification for subsequent adoption where the bank consulted BNM the first time without concerns, enhanced its framework, has independent assurance and confirmed incident response readiness. BNM may still direct a consultation.

bank.question: Under the Outsourcing policy document, what must the board approve each year before it is submitted to BNM?
options: Each outsourced staff member's employment contract
An outsourcing plan detailing planned outsourcing arrangements for the next financial year
The provider's annual financial statements
The provider's marketing materials
bank.explanation: Paragraph 8.5 requires the board to approve an outsourcing plan for the following financial year before it is submitted to BNM, with assurance from senior management.

bank.question: Why did BNM treat Bank of China (Malaysia) Berhad's relocation of two core banking systems to new data centres as needing prior approval?
options: The data centres were outside Malaysia and the law banned hosting core banking systems abroad
The systems were run by an unlicensed vendor
The relocation was done without informing customers
It was a significant change to an approved material outsourcing arrangement
bank.explanation: BNM's release said the relocation of core banking systems was a significant modification to an existing approved material outsourcing arrangement because it could materially change the level or type of risk.

bank.question: MCIPD requires outsourced service providers to train their personnel. What exactly must the bank ensure?
options: The provider trains its staff regularly on customer information and reviews it
The provider's staff attend the bank's induction once only, at the start of the contract, and sign the attendance sheet
The provider sends its training slides to BNM
The provider's staff hold a degree in data protection
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12.7 requires the bank to ensure the provider trains its personnel regularly on policies for proper handling of customer information and reviews the adequacy and effectiveness of that training.

bank.question: Under PDPA section 129 as amended, which of these is a basis on which a bank may transfer personal data outside Malaysia?
options: The overseas recipient is a well-known technology company
The data is encrypted, whatever the destination
The destination has a law substantially similar to the PDPA or ensures at least equivalent protection
The transfer is approved by the bank's marketing team
bank.explanation: Section 129(2) allows transfers where the place has a substantially similar law or ensures an adequate, at least equivalent, level of protection; section 129(3) lists further exceptions such as consent and contract performance.

bank.question: Under MCIPD, how often must senior management ensure an independent review of the effectiveness of customer information policies and controls?
options: At least once every five years
Only after a breach
At least once every two years
Every month
bank.explanation: Paragraph 9.8 requires an independent review at least once every two years; the reviewer can be an independent function such as internal audit.

bank.question: Which method does RMiT Appendix 12 list for evaluating the effectiveness of cyber awareness training at NCII entities?
options: Counting the number of posters displayed in branches
Post-programme quizzes or tests, participant feedback surveys and incident analysis during simulations
Asking BNM to grade the training materials
Measuring how long staff spend on the training page
bank.explanation: Paragraph 6.3.4 says effectiveness is evaluated on completion using post-programme assessments, feedback surveys and analysis of incidents during simulations; a pre-programme baseline may also be set.

bank.question: Which statement about the PDPA and MCIPD breach duties is correct for a Malaysian bank?
options: They run in parallel: notify BNM under MCIPD and the Commissioner under the PDPA
Notifying BNM replaces the duty to notify the PDP Commissioner, because BNM shares the notice with the Commissioner
Notifying the PDP Commissioner replaces the duty to notify BNM
Banks are exempt from the PDPA because of the FSA
bank.explanation: MCIPD's footnote reminds banks that, as data controllers, they must also comply with PDPA section 12B and the Commissioner's breach notification requirements effective 1 June 2025.
